findings.element: #b-edit-title, the "What it is" field in editor() (render-b.js:415-416); "Add a moment" in the owner bar (render-b.js:559, handler 515-518)
findings.problem: The first field in the panel the owner opens has no listener at all. Driven: opened owner-editing, filled the field with "Send the invitations to everyone", pressed Done. The row still reads "Send the invitations", the date line is unchanged, and the accessible name is still "Send the invitations, Saturday 8 August, in 23 days. Shown to guests. Open to change it." Nothing said the edit was dropped. Every other control in that panel is live, so the field reads as live, and it is the top field of the fifteen seconds this round was built for. One level up, the same class: "Add a moment" adds nothing. It calls openEditor on the first existing row, so the create verb opens a panel pre-filled with "Menu tasting at The Orchard" (7 items before the press, 7 after). With the title field dead there is no path in this direction by which an owner puts a new moment on the plan.
findings.fix: Give the field a writer beside setAway(). On the input at render-b.js:416 add on: { input: function (e) { var v = e.target.value.trim(); if (!v) return; record.title = v; var t = item.querySelector('.b-title'); t.setAttribute('data-full', v); t.textContent = v; var g = item.querySelector('.b-grab'); if (g) g.setAttribute('aria-label', grabLabel(record, item.getAttribute('data-date'), Number(item.getAttribute('data-away')), item.getAttribute('data-visibility') === 'hidden')); C.settle(); } } — settle() re-clamps the title word-safely and re-places the rows below it, so the measure stays true. For the bar, make name === "add" (render-b.js:515) build a real row: emit the same markup measure() builds with a fresh id, title "New moment" and data-away = 1, append it to .b-measure, call place(measureEl), then openEditor on it and focus #b-edit-title. If a real add is more than this round wants, replace act("Add a moment", …) at render-b.js:559 with inert("Adding comes next"), under this direction's own rule that nothing unbuilt is a button.

findings.element: the delete branch of wireOwner (render-b.js:503-509) and the reversibility bar .b-undo (render-b.js:276, paintUndo 283-309)
findings.problem: Driven at 1440x960: moved "Send the invitations" a week closer, then pressed "Delete this moment". Three things happen, all wrong. (1) document.activeElement becomes <body> — a keyboard owner who deleted a row seven rows down is dropped to the top of the document with no landmark. (2) Nothing is announced: the two role=status nodes are the stepper readout, which is removed along with the panel, and the undo bar, whose text does not change, so a screen-reader owner is told nothing at all happened. (3) The undo bar keeps standing there reading "Last change: Send the invitations moved 7 days closer." with its Undo button live — a live offer to restore a row that no longer exists. Press it and undo() pops the entry, querySelector('.b-item[data-id="…"]') returns null, nothing is restored, and the bar silently empties. So the one destructive action on the surface is the one action the one reversibility surface does not cover, and it makes a false claim in its place. lessons.md names this class twice ("Nothing reversible", "Repaints that annihilate place").
findings.fix: In render-b.js:503, before item.remove(), capture the row and push it onto the same history: history.push({ kind: 'delete', id: item.getAttribute('data-id'), title: record.title, html: item.outerHTML, next: item.nextElementSibling ? item.nextElementSibling.getAttribute('data-id') : null }), then paintUndo(root) so the bar reads "Last change: Send the invitations deleted." Branch undo() (render-b.js:481) on last.kind: for a delete, insert the saved node back into .b-measure before the recorded neighbour, call place(measureEl) and focus its .b-grab; for a move, keep the current path but if the item is not found do NOT pop the entry and do not clear the bar. In the delete handler, after item.remove(), focus the .b-grab of the next row, or the previous one if it was last, instead of letting focus fall to <body>. Give paintUndo a text branch for the delete kind so both kinds of change speak in the live region.

findings.element: openEditor (render-b.js:471-479) and .b-edit as a fixed bottom sheet (b.css:403-419)
findings.problem: Measured, not inferred. At 390x844 the state this round is graded on — owner-editing — opens with the edited row at y=996, 152px below the fold, while the sheet occupies 368px, 44% of the viewport. Tapping a row in owner-flight is no better: at 390, 768 and 1024 the row you just opened lands inside the sheet's band every time (at 390 the copy sits 485-558 against a sheet spanning 464-832). Nothing scrolls it into view and no band is reserved in layout, so the owner presses -7 and watches a figure change inside a panel while the object it moves is behind that panel or off screen — in the one direction whose entire thesis is that position IS the quantity. The keyboard route is the same defect in another form: Enter opens the panel and leaves focus on the row, and the panel is appended to .b-editHost (render-b.js:475), which sits upstream of the measure, so from the last row the forward Tab leaves the document altogether and the panel's first field is seven Shift+Tabs backwards.
findings.fix: At the end of openEditor (after render-b.js:478) add: var copy = item.querySelector('.b-copy'); var fixed = getComputedStyle(node).position === 'fixed'; var free = fixed ? node.getBoundingClientRect().top : window.innerHeight; var box = copy.getBoundingClientRect(); if (box.bottom > free - 16 || box.top < 16) window.scrollBy({ top: box.top - Math.max(16, (free - box.height) / 2), behavior: 'auto' }); then var first = node.querySelector('#b-edit-title'); if (first) first.focus(); — Escape and Done already return focus to the row (render-b.js:452-466), so the loop closes properly. Call the same three lines at the end of setAway (render-b.js:349, after place(measureEl)) so a stepped row is kept in the free band rather than driven under the sheet.

findings.problem: Three of the 262 assertions are true by construction, and one of them is already covering a live defect. (1) "every trim ends on a whole word" (307-310): its first conjunct is /\s\S*…$/.test(t.shown) === false ? true : true, which returns true either way; what is left is a prefix test that a mid-word cut ("…at The Orch…") passes just as happily, so the property the assertion is named after is not tested at all. (2) "no control advertises a verb it does not have" (541-550): the filter exempts every button carrying data-act, plus .b-grab, .b-step, .b-undoAct and anything inside .b-seg. Replayed in the browser that is 11 of 11 buttons on owner-flight and 1 of 1 on owner-empty — the array is empty whatever the code does. It also skips publish, the one state where the same filter DOES report something: "Send the link" and "Copy the link" (render-b.js:681) carry no data-act and no listener, and clicking both leaves document.body.innerHTML byte-identical, on the screen where the plan becomes theirs. (3) 573-577: inside else { ok(…, plate.position === "fixed") } the branch condition has already established exactly that, so at 390, 768 and 1024 the gate spends an assertion restating its own if and never checks what the sheet stands over — which is how the finding above survives a passing gate at three widths.
findings.fix: 307-310: assert the cut lands on a word boundary — const stem = t.shown.replace(/…$/, ''); t.full.startsWith(stem) && (t.full === t.shown || t.full[stem.length] === ' '). 541-550: drop the data-act exemption and prove each control instead — for every button in .b-field and .b-press, snapshot document.body.innerHTML plus the root's data-state, click, wait 250ms, and require that one of them changed; add "publish" and "owner-editing" to that state loop. 573-577: replace with the property the sheet actually owes — after openEditor, and again after one stepper press, assert the edited row's .b-copy rect is inside the viewport and does not intersect the .b-edit rect.

findings.problem: Measured in the browser at 1440x960. On the paper ground both resolve to ink at 0.46 over white: the empty state's date placeholder "3 October 2026" at 15px comes out at 3.13:1, and the disabled stepper glyph ("-7", after driving the item to its floor) at 3.13:1, against a 4.5:1 AA floor for that size. On ink the same token is 4.68:1 and legal. That asymmetry is the exact thing b.css states 180 lines earlier at .b-behindDate — "over ink, 0.46 is 4.65:1 and legal; over paper it is 3.15:1 and is not" — so the file writes the rule and then breaks it twice, and the code and its own comment disagree. Neither gate can see it: audit.mjs grades the default variant only (VARIANT = args.get("v") ?? config.defaultVariant, and the default is approach/ink), and even run with --v=paper it still passes, because ::placeholder is a pseudo-element it never enumerates and the disabled stepper only exists after a press it never makes. interaction-check.mjs opens the paper room exactly once, to read one background colour (583-590). The paper room is the light-lock reversal — the room that actually ships — and it is ungraded at all eleven states, with that placeholder the only place the expected date format is stated.
findings.fix: b.css:444 -> .b-input::placeholder { color: var(--fore-62); opacity: 1; } and b.css:464 -> .b-step[aria-disabled="true"] { color: var(--fore-62); border-color: var(--fore-16); } — 5.34:1 on paper, 7.4:1 on ink, still visibly quieter than a live glyph at --fore. Then close the hole: run audit.mjs twice more in the gate, with --v=paper and --v=record, and in interaction-check.mjs wrap the ground block (583-604) in a loop over config.variants that also asserts the computed colour of getComputedStyle(input, '::placeholder'), and of a driven .b-step[aria-disabled="true"], clears 4.5:1 against the composited .b-edit background.

biggestWin: The primary gesture is genuinely fixed, and it was every seat's worst finding last round. Driving it: one press of "Move a week earlier" moves the count, the date line under it, the row's accessible name, the readout, the gap sentence at the top of the page, the lead mark and the ceiling note all in the same frame, because setAway() is the only writer and every fact is derived from the one date it computes. The steppers do not move a pixel under the pointer, the page keeps its scroll position, and focus stays on the button that was pressed — through twenty presses into the ceiling, which states itself rather than absorbing the press. The measure stays strictly proportional at every width, and the tick and the count stay on the true pixel while only the words are pushed clear, so a crowded pair never restates one item's distance as another's. That is studio-grade work and it is what the rest of the score is standing on. What is left in the owner's panel is not the gesture, it is the controls arranged around it: an inert title field, a delete with no way back, a create verb that creates nothing, two dead buttons in the publish ceremony, and a panel that opens away from the row it edits. That is one focused build of roughly a day, not a different decision, and it is the whole distance between 7.4 and the gate.
